form.current-chamber: IN THE SENATE OF THE UNITED STATES

action.action-desc: Mr. Reed (for himself, Mr. Scott of South Carolina, Mr. Whitehouse, Mrs. Blackburn, Mr. Durbin, Mr. Cassidy, Ms. Hassan, Ms. Ernst, Mr. Wicker, Mr. Coons, Mr. Barrasso, Mr. Crapo, Mr. Tillis, Mrs. Murray, Mr. Marshall, Mr. Young, Mr. Cardin, Mr. Manchin, Mr. Braun, Mr. Daines, Ms. Rosen, Mr. Boozman, Ms. Lummis, and Mr. Peters) submitted the following resolution; which was considered and agreed to

form.official-title: Designating April 2021 as Financial Literacy Month.

whereas.text: Whereas, according to the 2019 report entitled Economic Well-Being of U.S. Households by the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, 37 percent of adults in the United States cannot cover an unexpected expense of $400;

Whereas, according to the 2019 report entitled “How America Banks: Household Use of Banking and Financial Services” by the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation, approximately 5.4 percent of households in the United States are unbanked and, therefore, have limited or no access to savings, lending, and other basic financial services;
Whereas, according to the 2020 Consumer Financial Literacy Survey final report of the National Foundation for Credit Counseling that was conducted prior to COVID–19 lockdowns—

paragraph.text: a majority (62 percent) of adults in the United States had credit card debt during the 1-year period ending on the date of publication of the report;
over 2/5 (43 percent) of adults in the United States carry credit card debt from month to month; and
approximately 47 percent of adults in the United States maintain a budget;

whereas.text: Whereas, according to the statistical release of the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System for the fourth quarter of 2020 entitled Household Debt and Credit—

paragraph.text: outstanding household debt in the United States has been increasing steadily since 2013 and was $414,000,000,000 higher than at the end of 2019; and
outstanding student loan balances have more than doubled in the last decade to approximately $1,560,000,000,000;

whereas.text: Whereas, according to the 2020 report entitled Survey of the States: Economic and Personal Finance Education in Our Nation’s Schools, by the Council for Economic Education—

paragraph.text: only 25 States require students to take an economics course as a high school graduation requirement; and
only 21 States require students to take a personal finance course as a high school graduation requirement, either independently or as part of an economics course;

whereas.text: Whereas, according to the Gallup-HOPE Index, in 2016 only 57 percent of students in the United States had money in a bank or credit union account;
Whereas expanding access to the safe, mainstream financial system will provide individuals with less expensive and more secure options for managing finances and building wealth;
Whereas quality personal financial education is essential to ensure that individuals are prepared—

paragraph.text: to manage money, credit, and debt; and
to become responsible workers, heads of household, investors, entrepreneurs, business leaders, and citizens;
empowers individuals to make wise financial decisions; and
reduces the confusion caused by an increasingly complex economy;

whereas.text: Whereas a greater understanding of, and familiarity with, financial markets and institutions will lead to increased economic activity and growth; and

paragraph.text: determined that coordinating Federal financial literacy efforts and formulating a national strategy is important; and

in light of that determination, passed the Financial Literacy and Education Improvement Act (20 U.S.C. 9701 et seq.), establishing the Financial Literacy and Education Commission: Now, therefore, be it
designates April 2021 as Financial Literacy Month to raise public awareness about—

subparagraph.text: the importance of personal financial education in the United States; and
the serious consequences that may result from a lack of understanding about personal finances; and

paragraph.text: calls on the Federal Government, States, localities, schools, nonprofit organizations, businesses, and the people of the United States to observe Financial Literacy Month with appropriate programs and activities.
